'''Maria Adelaide Sneider''' (6 December 1937 – 1 May 1989)<ref name="deathdate"/> (also known as '''Maria Adelaide Sneider Ludovici''', her second [[surname]] being "Ludovici")<ref>As she signes herself in {{harv|Sneider Ludovici|1970}} and in several other of her scientific works: see also the "Author index" in {{Harv|Fichera|1974|p=202}}.</ref> was an [[Italia]]n [[mathematician]] working on [[numerical analysis|numerical]] and [[mathematical analysis]]. She is known for her work on the [[Capacity of a set|theory of electrostatic capacities]] of non-smooth [[Closed set|closed]] [[hypersurface]]s:<ref>According to {{harvtxt|Fichera|1990|p=395}}: see also her work {{harv|Sneider Ludovici|1970}}, the associated report {{harv|Picone|Tricomi|Fichera|1970}}, and the introductory remarks in {{harv|Hayman|1993|p=119}}.</ref> Apart from the development of precise estimates for the [[numerical approximation]] of the electrostatic [[Capacitance#Capacitance of simple systems|capacity]] of the unit [[cube]],<ref>See {{harv|Picone|Tricomi|Fichera|1970}}, {{Harv|Fichera|1990|p=396}} and {{harv|Hayman|1993|p=119}}.</ref> this work also led her to give a rigorous proof of [[Green's identities]] for large classes of hypersurfaces with singularities,<ref>See {{Harv|Fichera|1974|pp=178–179}} and {{Harv|Fichera|1990|pp.=396–397}}.</ref> and later to develop an accurate mathematical analysis of the [[points effect]].<ref>See {{harvtxt|Fichera|1990|pp=398–400}}.</ref> She is also known for her contributions to the [[Dirichlet problem]] for [[pluriharmonic function]]s on the unit [[sphere]] of <math>\mathbb{C}^n.</math><ref>{{Harv|Fichera|1990|p=405}}.</ref>

==Work==
{{quote
|text= [[Gaetano Fichera|Gaetano]] and his former student Adelaide Sneider have done important work on capacity and in particular on the capacity of a cube and the corresponding potential fields.
|sign= [[Walter Kurt Hayman|Walter K. Hayman]]
|source= {{harv|Hayman|1993|p=119}}.
}}
